findings.text: the census citation pair is off by one and contradicts itself within one parenthetical: `:33` is offered as START but census.py:33 is END = "2026-09-26T10:00:00Z" (START is census.py:32) and `:34` is offered as END but census.py:34 is `PROJECTS = {`, which the same parenthetical also cites as `:34-40 PROJECTS->branch map`; an implementer of the-fleet-reports-its-velocity §2 navigating the port source by these anchors lands on the wrong constants, and the run's gate cannot catch it because it checks existence and EOF, not content.

the window-argument citation is off by one as well: the row states the only window-ish argument on the tool is `since` (`reckon/mcp.py:3633`), but `since` is declared at reckon/mcp.py:3634 and :3633 declares `plan`; the claim itself verifies, so this is a mechanical correction to a map whose value is that its citations are followable, and it is the same defect mode as the census pair above.

the follow_on attributing the misspelling 'recknon' to "this node's dispatch preamble" is false: prompt.txt spells the repository name 'reckon' in all 15 of its occurrences and contains no 'recknon', and the delivered reuse-map.md contains none either — the run's own stream.jsonl shows the misspelling was in the worker's own draft (its report text "no recknon code is implicated" and its manifest evidence_inputs "recknon/crew/promotion.py"), repaired by the node's own edits before delivery ("fixed; ... recknon remaining: 1", the survivor being this follow_on sentence itself) — so the recommended spellcheck pass on the S25 dispatch templates would chase a defect no dispatch carries.

item_verdicts.diff: There is no diff to read: `git -C .../s25-reuse-map-review-and-velocity rev-parse HEAD` is 9945557624511d329211b5b573cdf77d38b02ac4, equal to the dispatch base, and the tree is clean, so the landed change is the report on disk (23,419 bytes, three rows) plus the run-directory gate and driver, which is the change I read - the node was fenced to a deliverable outside the repository and wrote no code in it.
item_verdicts.done_when: The done_when asks for exactly one row per named section, four answered sub-parts per row, citations at the dispatch base, and a manifest naming the base sha and the row count; the run's gate reuse-map-gate.py asserts the row count, five columns with content, every citation inside its file's EOF, and a 2-of-2 positive control, its log records PASS with 58/58 resolved at 99455576, and I re-ran the gate independently at the same revision (review-gate-rerun.log) reproducing PASS - noting that the citation rule it implements checks a cited line exists at or below EOF rather than that the named symbol sits on it, which is why the two miscitations in reuse-map.md:13 pass.
item_verdicts.goal: The goal asks for a map of the reuse candidates for the review-tier and velocity sections of the S25 first wave, and reuse-map.md:9-13 carries exactly one row for each named section - a-review-is-sized-to-its-risk §2 and §6 and the-fleet-reports-its-velocity §2 - each row giving candidate modules, symbols and tests as file:line with a one-line fitness verdict; I read the cited lines at base 99455576 in the reviewed run's worktree (flight.py:45, flight.yaml:644, promotion.py:2676, ledger.py:99/120, project_state.py:2088, census.py:79/141, mcp.py:3629, cli.py:782, summary.json window among them) and every one resolves to the named symbol except the census START/END pair cited at reuse-map.md:13, which is off by one.
item_verdicts.manifest: Read /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20260926T205140532761-s25-reuse-map-review-and-velocity/manifest.md; `reckon crew check-manifest --run r-20260926T205140532761-s25-reuse-map-review-and-velocity` returns ok true with no findings, and its load-bearing numbers (base sha 99455576, 3 rows, gate PASS with 58 resolved citations and the 2/2 positive control) match the manifest's own logs and my independent re-run; its follow_on (1), however, misattributes the run's self-corrected draft typo 'recknon' to the dispatch preamble (third finding), which check-manifest itself does not audit.
item_verdicts.write_paths: The single declared path is the report /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/reports/reckon/s25-coord/s25-reuse-map-review-and-velocity/reuse-map.md; the reviewed worktree sits at the base sha 9945557624511d329211b5b573cdf77d38b02ac4 with an empty `git status --porcelain` and no commits, so the repository carries no part of the change, the gate script, negative-control driver and logs live under the run's own directory as the dispatch's named log location, and the /tmp scratch trees the negative control mutated are gone.

justifications.durability: reuse-map-gate.py fails on a deleted row and on a citation moved past EOF, both demonstrated red in reuse-map-negative-control.log against scratch copies, but the guard lives only in the run directory, nothing in the repository re-runs it, and a citation landing on the wrong existing line (the pair in reuse-map.md:13) passes it.
justifications.evidence: The gate's result is recorded rather than claimed (reuse-map-gate.log shows PASS, 58 resolved, 2/2 positive control at 99455576) and its negative control shows two mutations reddened it, and I reproduced the PASS independently, but its citation rule resolves existence and EOF only, so "58 resolved" is consistent with the two miscitations at reuse-map.md:13 and measures less than a reader would take from it.
justifications.fit: The report follows the required four-answer row shape and closes with a method section naming its instrument, its positive controls and the one claim it could not check (reuse-map.md:15-29), and the run's two Python files are named by capability with no plan label, version suffix or changelog prose (naming checks run clean).
justifications.goal_fidelity: All three rows are present and their substance verifies at the base (census.py:141 path_class, promotion.py:474, ledger.py:1431, dispatch.py:4145, project_state.py:2088 all say what the row says), but the port anchors in reuse-map.md:13 cite `:33` for START and `:34` for END when START is census.py:32 and END census.py:33, so the map's most load-bearing citations for the port it exists to seed are wrong.
justifications.scope_discipline: The deliverable is the one declared path outside the repository, `git status --porcelain` in the reviewed worktree is empty at the base sha with no commits, and the only other artefacts are the gate, driver and logs under the run's own directory, which the dispatch names as the log location.
